headline: `b.guardCsv` reads a document under every delimiter a consumer might use, and its sanitize disarms or refuses
summary: The CSV guard split cells on every delimiter it knows at once, while a consumer reads with one, so a formula cell that a comma reader or a tab reader sees could sit inside a cell the guard read as quoted. Each candidate delimiter is now its own reading and every finding any reading produces is reported. `sanitize()` never disarmed a formula cell and returned one the operator had set to refuse; it now disarms under a prefixing policy and refuses under `reject` and for a denylisted function. The profiles' default mitigation moves from a TAB prefix to the single-quote prefix, which holds under every delimiter reading. Upgrading requires no code change; a CSV emitted through the guard carries `'` where it carried a TAB in front of a formula-shaped cell, and `prefix-tab` remains selectable for tab-separated output.

items.title: `b.guardCsv` reads a document under each delimiter separately
items.body:
The cell walk treated `,`, `;`, TAB and `|` as delimiters at the same time. A consumer reads with one of them, and the two structures differ around quotes: to a comma reader `a;"x` followed by a newline and `""=1` is text, a record end, and then an empty quoted section with `=1` after it, which every RFC 4180 reader including `b.csv.parse` yields as the cell `=1`, a live formula. The guard split at the `;`, read the quote as opening a quoted cell, and carried that cell across the newline, so the formula rule never saw the cell and strict validation reported nothing. The same shape hid from the guard behind a TAB or a `|` a comma reader does not split on, and behind a comma a tab reader does not.

The guard now walks the document once per candidate delimiter (`,`, `;`, TAB, `|`, and the operator's own) and reports what any reading finds: a formula cell, a denylisted function, and the residual check that decides whether a sanitized document can be served. One cell is one finding however many readings expose it.

items.title: `b.guardCsv.sanitize` disarms a formula cell or refuses it
items.body:
`sanitize()` stripped characters and returned the document, so a formula cell came back as written, under `formulaInjectionPolicy: "reject"` too, and a denylisted `=WEBSERVICE(...)` came back as written at every profile, while the function's own documentation promised it never returns a class the operator asked it to refuse. It now refuses a formula cell under `reject`, a denylisted function, and mixed line endings under `dialectPolicy: "strict"`, each with the finding's rule id. Under a prefixing policy it disarms a formula cell the way the gate does: the document is re-parsed, re-serialized with the prefix inside a quoted field, and read again under every delimiter; a cell that is still a formula under one of those readings is refused rather than served. The gate serves what `sanitize` returns.

The mitigated form of a denylisted function is still the denylisted function. `"'=WEBSERVICE(...)"` and, under `prefix-tab`, `"<TAB>=WEBSERVICE(...)"` validated clean; Excel drops the leading apostrophe when it saves and re-opens the file, and the gate refuses a denylisted call even prefixed. The denylist walk reads through the guard's own prefixes now.

items.title: The profiles' formula mitigation is `prefix-quote`
items.body:
`strict`, `balanced` and `permissive` prefixed a formula-shaped cell with a TAB inside the quoted field. A TAB is the delimiter of a tab-separated reader, and such a reader of a comma document with more than one column takes the quote and comma before the TAB as text and splits at the TAB: `b.csv.parse` with `delimiter: "\t"` reads `"alice","<TAB>=cmd|x"` as the cells `alice,"` and `=cmd|x"`, a live formula. The single-quote prefix holds under every delimiter reading and is the mitigation OWASP lists first. OWASP also notes that Excel drops it when it saves and re-opens the file, so the TAB prefix remains selectable as `formulaInjectionPolicy: "prefix-tab"` for tab-separated output, where it holds. A document sanitized under `prefix-tab` that a tab-separated reading would still evaluate is refused rather than served as disarmed.

`|` is no longer a formula trigger: no spreadsheet evaluator opens a formula on it and it is on no published list, so a cell such as `|x` is emitted as it is and is not a finding. A leading TAB, CR or LF is read through to the character after it, as an importer that trims leading whitespace evaluates what follows: `<TAB>=cmd` is a formula and `<TAB>hello` is text, which also stops a tab-separated file whose first cell is an empty quoted section from being refused under the comma reading. Text after a closing quote is read as part of the cell, as the parsers read it.
